name: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (Maharashtra top-up to PM-KISAN)
amount: ₹6,000 a year in 3 instalments (a rise to ₹9,000 was reported in Feb 2025 — confirm the current amount on the official portal)
description: Maharashtra government's additional income support for farmer families who already receive PM-KISAN. Launched in October 2023.
benefits: Extra money every year, paid in three instalments by DBT on top of the ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN.
eligibility_text: Farmer families of Maharashtra who are PM-KISAN beneficiaries, with cultivable land in their name and an Aadhaar-linked bank account. You must first be registered on the PM-KISAN portal.
steps: Register on the PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) and finish eKYC.
Make sure your Aadhaar-linked bank account and land details are correct.
Check your payment status on the Namo Shetkari portal.

name: MahaDBT Farmer Schemes (Maharashtra online portal)
amount: Varies by scheme: machinery subsidy is typically 40–50%; micro-irrigation 45–55%
description: Maharashtra's single online portal for farmer schemes such as agricultural mechanization (including tractors and other farm machinery), micro-irrigation and other agriculture department subsidies. You register once and apply to individual schemes from your login.
benefits: Subsidy is paid directly to the farmer's bank account after the purchase or installation is verified.
eligibility_text: Farmers resident in Maharashtra with land records and an Aadhaar-linked bank account. Each scheme on the portal has its own conditions, and SC/ST, women and small/marginal farmers get priority or a higher rate in many of them.
required_documents: Quotation or invoice for the item, as the scheme requires
steps: Go to mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in and register or log in as a farmer.
Complete your profile with Aadhaar, land and bank details.
Open the Farmer Schemes section and choose a scheme, for example Agricultural Mechanization.
Fill in the form, upload documents and submit.
Track your application from your login and follow the instructions if you are selected.

name: Mukhyamantri Saur Krushi Pump Yojana (PM-KUSUM in Maharashtra)
amount: Large subsidy on 3, 5 and 7.5 HP solar pumps; farmer's share reported as about 10% — confirm with MSEDCL
description: Maharashtra's way of running PM-KUSUM solar pumps for farmers, with pump sizes of 3, 5 and 7.5 HP. Applications go through the state's power distribution company.
benefits: Central and state subsidy covers most of the pump cost; the farmer pays a small share. Exact shares and category-wise amounts are on the state notification.
eligibility_text: Maharashtra farmers who need a solar irrigation pump and meet the state's conditions. Some areas, for example where groundwater is restricted, can be excluded, so check your village with your MSEDCL or taluka agriculture office.
required_documents: Caste certificate (if claiming a category rate)
steps: Open pmkusum.mnre.gov.in and follow the Maharashtra link, or ask your MSEDCL or taluka agriculture office where applications are open.
Register and fill in the application with your land and water-source details.
Pay your share when you receive the demand note.
The vendor installs the pump and it is inspected.
source_organization: MSEDCL / Government of Maharashtra under MNRE's PM-KUSUM

name: Crop insurance in Maharashtra (PMFBY farmer share from 2025)
amount: Standard PMFBY share: 2% (Kharif), 1.5% (Rabi food crops and oilseeds), 5% (commercial/horticulture)
description: Maharashtra stopped the arrangement in which the state paid the whole farmer share of the PMFBY premium in 2025, according to a Government of India release of August 2026. Farmers therefore pay the normal PMFBY share. Enrolment in Kharif 2025 fell sharply because of this.
benefits: Same cover as PMFBY: notified crops in notified areas, with claims paid to the farmer's bank account.
eligibility_text: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas of Maharashtra, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers. The state sets the last date for each crop and season.
required_documents: Land record (7/12) or tenancy / sharecropping agreement
steps: Check the last date for your crop and district on pmfby.gov.in or at your taluka agriculture office.
Enrol through your bank, a CSC, or yourself on pmfby.gov.in.
Pay your share of the premium and keep the receipt.
Report crop loss within 72 hours of a localised calamity.
source_organization: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
